log.why: E9 splits the prior mass nearly 50/50 (0.510 vs 0.491) while separating top contenders lacZ and hisG.
Treating at 1 uM splits Ticket 2's prior nearly in half (0.418 vs 0.582), maximizing information while Ticket 1 incubates.
E1 directly tests the leading candidate hisG (0.633) against runner-up trpE (0.265) for decisive resolution.
Testing at 3 µM best bisects the remaining dose posterior (0.388 vs 0.612) while Ticket 1 awaits E1.
Treating at 10 µM splits the remaining threshold probability nearly in half (0.475 vs 0.525) and incubates while we publish Ticket 1.
hisG has a 0.951 posterior after E1 lost the phenotype, making immediate publication high-value and freeing a ticket slot.
Ticket 3 needs urgent evidence and E10 splits the prior mass nearly evenly (0.536 vs 0.464) while utilizing a free incubator before publishing Ticket 2.
Testing {rpoB, ftsZ} splits Ticket 4's prior nearly in half (0.459) and incubates in parallel while we next publish Ticket 2.
Start E11 on Ticket 3 to separate recA from araC/ftsZ while leaving time to publish expiring Ticket 2 during incubation.
Ticket 2 has only 9 seconds left and a strong 0.767 posterior for 10 uM, so publish now before expiration.
Ticket 3 has only 8 seconds left, so we must publish the leading candidate araC (0.597) before it expires.
Ticket 4 has 25 s left and is split between rpoB and ftsZ; knocking out ftsZ resolves the tie before expiration.
Testing 1 µM splits Ticket 5's posterior mass nearly in half while Ticket 4's decisive ftsZ knockout finishes incubating.
Two positive knockouts give ftsZ a 0.901 posterior, and with 1 second left we must immediately submit.
Testing 3 µM directly separates the leading 3 µM hypothesis from 10 µM and higher doses before publishing.
While waiting 6 s for Ticket 5's E3, testing top candidate trpE on Ticket 6 enables a high-confidence second publication before time expires.
With one second left in the round, no new plates can finish, and trpE has a strong 0.772 posterior from E5.
